request: A motion promo for the LitClaude README, just like a pro typography motion artist's reel at its best, about what this product really does.
pathReason: The film has to show drawn things (a terminal, a goal card, a small web page being clicked, a record handed to a new session), so the visuals are authored as a page and captured frame by frame; type alone cannot show them.
idea: One small job goes through the whole loop on screen: asked for in a prompt, pinned as a goal with checks that fail first, checked on a real page by clicking it, then written into a record that a fresh session opens and continues from.
audience: Developers who already use Claude Code and lose the thread between sessions.
channel: The top of a GitHub README, autoplaying muted as an animated preview, with the MP4 one click away.
formatReason: A README column and the MP4 link both show a landscape frame, and the terminal and browser panels read best wide.

beats.onScreen: Headline ASK FOR THE WORK. on the left, already settled in the first frame. On the right a terminal panel wipes in and a to-do-list prompt types itself, ending in a lime lit; the step row along the bottom sits unlit.
beats.motion: Panel wipes in from the left, characters type at a steady pace, a cursor blinks in lime, the headline lines rise from a mask.
beats.sound: pad and pulse only, unhurried, the room settling

beats.purpose: Context: the goal is pinned and the checks fail first
beats.onScreen: Headline PIN THE GOAL. with the line WRITE THE FAILING TEST FIRST under it. The terminal panel grows into a goal card: the job in one line, then three rows (add, complete, delete), each with an orange cross drawn in. The Plan step lights.
beats.motion: Match cut: the panel keeps its frame and grows taller while its content swaps; rows slide in on a stagger; crosses draw with a stroke.
beats.sound: hit on the cut as the terminal becomes the goal card

beats.purpose: Key moment: the real page is checked
beats.onScreen: Headline CHECK THE REAL PAGE. A small to-do page drops in above; a cursor clicks Add, then the checkbox, then the delete cross, and the three crosses in the strip below turn into lime ticks one by one. Build then Check light up.
beats.motion: The goal card shrinks into a strip while the page reveals from the top; a cursor glides between targets with a click ring at each; ticks draw in.
beats.sound: hit on the cut, then a rise under the clicks into the handoff

beats.purpose: Details: the record is handed to the next session
beats.onScreen: Headline HAND IT OFF. with the line about the next session under it. The strip grows into a record card listing the goal, what was checked and the next step, with the project folder named. A lime spark travels down a line into a fresh terminal whose prompt asks to read the handoff.
beats.motion: Strip grows into the card, spark follows a drawn line, the new terminal wipes in and types.
beats.sound: hit on the cut, rise as the record travels into the new session

beats.onScreen: The right column clears. Headline KEEP THE WORK LIT. with LIT in orange, the line naming Claude Code, and the install command in lime mono. A large flame ignites on the right above a status bar; all four steps sit lit.
beats.motion: Panels clip away, the flame springs up and flickers, rings expand once, LIT glows.
beats.sound: hit on the cut, cadence on the final line, resolve into the last chord

subject.name: LitClaude
specifics: a Claude Code plugin that plans, builds and checks work
leaves a record in the project that the next session reads
its status bar carries a flame and the name

typePlan.hierarchy: Archivo 900 uppercase headlines at about 116 px on the left, Pretendard for the supporting line, mono for everything a terminal would print, Silkscreen for small labels; one accent word per headline.

sound.plan: A warm keyed bed at a walking tempo, with a hit on each of the four cuts, one rise into the handoff and a cadence on the closing line.

lines: Build a to-do list in a single HTML file. lit
The next session reads the record and carries on.
Read the handoff. What is next?
Plan, build and check your work in Claude Code.

inventions: The demo job: a to-do list in one HTML file (taken from the README's own quick start) with its three checks add, complete and delete.
The example record contents: the goal line, the checked list and the next step 'keyboard shortcuts'.
The second session's prompt, 'Read the handoff. What is next?', which follows the README's advice to ask Claude to read the file and name the next action.
All copy lines and the on-screen terminal, page and card drawings.
ambition: A reel-grade explainer where one continuous object, the panel, changes state across four cuts (terminal, goal card, checklist strip, record), the type has one clear hierarchy with a mask-rise entry and a readable hold, the cursor clicks land on exact frames, and the last frame is a flame lighting the same status bar the product installs.
